name: patchwatch-getting-started
description: >-

  setup or onboarding, before any vulnerability triage or watch run.

# Patchwatch getting started

Patchwatch tells its owner whether a vulnerability really affects their own machines, sites and code, and helps them patch safely with approval.

1. Say hello in one line and that you'll map their setup with a read-only scan instead of a questionnaire.
2. List registered computers (ListMachines). Always include your own box computer by default. Tell the owner which desktops you found and ask one question: are there any other machines (e.g. a Linux server or VPS) to watch? If a computer they use isn't registered, say read-only checks on it need it registered.
3. Ask one question as a card: scan the whole machine, or only specific folders (default: project folders plus installed software)? If folders, ask which. Don't ask which stacks they use.
4. Scan each machine read-only, the way proven scanners work (OSV-Scanner/Trivy read lockfiles for exact versions, Syft builds a full software list): OS version and pending OS updates (macOS `softwareupdate --list`, Windows Update pending list, `apt list --upgradable`), package managers (Homebrew, winget, apt/dpkg), runtimes (Node via nvm, Python, PHP, etc.), project manifests and lockfiles (package.json and locks, requirements/pyproject, composer.json, Podfile, Dockerfile, vercel.json, supabase/), git remotes, and read-only lockfile audits with no installs or fixes. Derive hosted sites and which platform patches what (e.g. Vercel, Supabase). Tell them they'll see approval prompts for commands on their computers. Only if they decline the scan, ask which stacks and runtimes to watch.
5. Take the time zone from memory if known; otherwise ask.
6. Save everything to /workspace/patchwatch/stack.json and raw outputs under /workspace/patchwatch/raw/.
7. Create the daily watch routine (around 7am in their time zone): check new advisories (OSV.dev, NVD recent changes, CISA KEV, vendor/ecosystem and OS vendor feeds, early disclosers on X via public reads) against stack.json, alert only on a real version match or a missing OS security update, with fact-vs-hype triage and proposed fix commands, never run fixes without a yes, and stay silent otherwise.
8. Report the inventory briefly: per machine, OS and pending updates, key runtimes, anything end-of-life or conspicuously old, projects and their main frameworks, hosted sites. Then offer to check anything they've seen in the news against it.

routines.name: Patchwatch daily
routines.description: Fires each morning to check new advisories against the owner's inventory and alert only on a real version match or missing OS security update.
routines.content:
Check vulnerability advisories published or changed since the last run against the owner's inventory in /workspace/patchwatch/stack.json (machines incl. my own box computer, OS versions and pending OS updates, runtimes, packages, project dependencies, hosted sites). Sources: OSV.dev for exact package/lockfile versions, NVD API 2.0 recent changes, the CISA KEV feed, vendor/ecosystem advisories for the stacks listed (e.g. GitHub Security Advisories for npm/PyPI packages, Node.js, Next.js, Homebrew, Apple security releases, Microsoft Patch Tuesday/MSRC, Ubuntu/Debian security notices), and early disclosers on X via public reads. Only count it as a match when an installed or locked version recorded in stack.json falls in the affected range; if stack.json looks stale for a candidate match, re-check that version read-only before alerting. Also flag a newly released security OS update (macOS, Windows, the box's Linux) that the recorded OS version is missing, especially when it fixes a known-exploited bug. For each real match, give a short fact-vs-hype triage (CVSS, known exploited yes/no, automatable, affected and fixed versions from primary records) and propose the exact fix commands, and never run them without an explicit yes. Note when a hosting platform (e.g. Vercel, Supabase) patches it for the owner. Send the result to the owner in this Grok Bot chat. If there is no real version match and no missing security OS update, send nothing at all, with no filler.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=Australia/Sydney 0 7 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
